acf.scripture_text: “Whoever says he is in the light and hates his brother is still in darkness. Whoever loves his brother abides in the light, and in him there is no cause for stumbling. But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.”
acf.body_content:
John has strikingly described the love commandment as both old and new (1 John 2:7–8). It is old because it was given to the people of God long before the Apostles wrote. It is new because in Jesus Christ it has taken on a fullness and a power that mark a new era in redemptive history. In today’s passage, John applies this commandment directly to his readers, framing love for the brethren as a test by which the reality of one’s place in the light of Christ may be examined (vv. 9–11).

The structure of these three verses turns on the contrast between two professions and two conditions.
acf.coram_deo: Examine yourself today by John’s love test. Toward whom in the household of faith do you carry resentment, contempt, or settled coldness?
